knowledge_statements.title: Parametric Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Principal-sequence method for continuous separable convex optimization over a polymatroid base.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:2^E\to\mathbb R\) be normalized, nondecreasing, and submodular, and let \(w\in\mathbb R_{++}^E\). For each parameter \(\lambda\in\mathbb R\), compute the inclusionwise maximal minimizer \(S_\lambda\) of \(f(S)-\lambda w(S)\) over \(S\subseteq E\). Enumerate the finitely many breakpoints at which \(S_\lambda\) changes, obtaining a nested chain \(\varnothing=S_0\subsetneq S_1\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq S_k=E\). Assign the breakpoint value \(\lambda_j\) to every element of \(S_j\setminus S_{j-1}\), and output \(x_i=w_i\lambda_j\) for those elements. The resulting vector is the weighted lexicographically optimal base and minimizes \(\sum_{i\in E}x_i^2/(2w_i)\) over \(B(f)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Find maximal minimizers of a parametric submodular function, extract their nested breakpoints, and assign each block its breakpoint ratio to obtain the weighted lexicographically optimal base.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\in B(f)\) minimizes \(\sum_{i\in E}x_i^2/(2w_i)\) and is weighted lexicographically optimal.

notation.meaning: The base polytope defined by x(S)≤f(S) for all S and x(E)=f(E).
The sum of weights over S.
The inclusionwise maximal minimizer at parameter λ.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm content kind fits the Parametric Methods leaf, and the statement is internally coherent, but no citation is supplied. An authoritative source with a specific theorem, section, or page must verify the breakpoint convention, endpoint handling, block assignment, and identification with both weighted lexicographic optimality and quadratic minimization.

children.title: Parametric Decomposition Structure
children.top_down_role: Connections between parameter breakpoints and decomposition chains.

knowledge_statements.title: Parametric Decomposition Structure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nested maximal minimizers and breakpoint blocks of a parametric submodular family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:2^E\to\mathbb R\) be submodular and \(w\in\mathbb R_{++}^E\). For \(\lambda\in\mathbb R\), let \(S_\lambda\) be the inclusionwise maximal minimizer of \(f(S)-\lambda w(S)\). If \(\lambda<\mu\), then \(S_\lambda\subseteq S_\mu\). Consequently, only finitely many distinct maximal minimizers occur, and they form a chain \(\varnothing=S_0\subsetneq S_1\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq S_k=E\), after adjoining the limiting endpoints when necessary. Each difference \(S_j\setminus S_{j-1}\) is a decomposition block, and the parameter at which it enters is its critical value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Maximal minimizers of the parametric submodular functions are nested as the parameter increases, producing a finite chain of critical blocks.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lambda<\mu\Longrightarrow S_\lambda\subseteq S_\mu\), so the distinct \(S_\lambda\) form a finite chain.

notation.meaning: The inclusionwise maximal minimizer of the parameterized set function.
The sum of positive element weights over S.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property content kind matches the structural leaf. Nestedness of maximal minimizers is standard, but the record has no inspectable citation, and the precise treatment of empty and full limiting sets and critical values requires source verification.

knowledge_statements.title: Lexicographically Optimal Bases
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weighted continuous lexicographic optimality on a polymatroid base.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:2^E\to\mathbb R\) be normalized, nondecreasing, and submodular, and let \(w\in\mathbb R_{++}^E\). For \(x\in B(f)\), arrange the ratios \(x_i/w_i\) in nondecreasing order. There exists a unique base \(x^*\in B(f)\) whose ordered ratio vector is lexicographically maximal. The same base is the unique minimizer of the strictly convex objective \(\sum_{i\in E}x_i^2/(2w_i)\) over \(B(f)\). Its ratio levels are constant on the blocks of the parametric decomposition generated by minimizers of \(f(S)-\lambda w(S)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A polymatroid base has a unique weighted lexicographically maximal ratio vector; its base uniquely minimizes weighted squared norm and is constant by parametric blocks.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^*=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in B(f)}\sum_{i\in E}x_i^2/(2w_i)\), and \(x^*\) is weighted lexicographically optimal.

notation.meaning: The polymatroid base polytope of f.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem content kind fits the topic, but no source supports the asserted uniqueness, the chosen nondecreasing lexicographic convention, the quadratic characterization, or the parametric-block characterization. These linked conclusions require an authoritative theorem locator.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Linear-Weight Lexicographic Bases as Weighted Minimum-Norm Bases
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive linear-weight specialization and its separable quadratic representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $w(e)>0$ for every $e\in E$ and define $h_e(t)=t/w(e)$. A lexicographically optimal base with respect to $w$ lexicographically maximizes the nondecreasing ordering of $(x(e)/w(e))_{e\in E}$. Its solution set equals that of the weighted quadratic problem $\min\{\sum_{e\in E}x(e)^2/w(e):x\in\mathrm B(f)\}$, which is a weighted minimum-norm base problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With positive weights, lexicographically maximizing the sorted ratios x(e)/w(e) is equivalent to minimizing the weighted quadratic norm over the base polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname*{arg\,lexmax}_{x\in\mathrm B(f)}\mathrm T\bigl((x(e)/w(e))_{e\in E}\bigr)=\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{x\in\mathrm B(f)}\sum_{e\in E}\frac{x(e)^2}{w(e)}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Subdifferential Characterization from a Lexicographically Optimal Base
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes scaled-weight subdifferential membership by threshold containment and tightness for the lexicographically optimal base.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x^*\) be the lexicographically optimal base of \((\mathcal D,f)\) with respect to \(w\). For \(\lambda\in\mathbb R\), define \(B_\lambda^+=\{e\in E:x^*(e)\leq \lambda w(e)\}\) and \(B_\lambda^-=\{e\in E:x^*(e)<\lambda w(e)\}\). knowledge_statements.statement_title: Equivalent Characterizations of Nonlinearly Weighted Lexicographic Base Optimality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tight-level-set, dependence-set, and separable-optimization characterizations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume the nonlinear weights $h_e$ satisfy the standing continuity, monotonicity, and surjectivity conditions. Let $x\in\mathrm B(f)$, define $\eta(e)=h_e(x(e))$, let $\eta_1<\cdots<\eta_p$ be the distinct values of $\eta$, and put $A_i=\{e\in E:\eta(e)\leq\eta_i\}$. Then the following are equivalent: (i) $x$ is lexicographically optimal with respect to $(h_e)_{e\in E}$; (ii) $A_i\in\mathcal D$ and $x(A_i)=f(A_i)$ for every $i$; (iii) $\operatorname{dep}(x,e)\subseteq A_i$ for every $i$ and every $e\in A_i$; and (iv) $x$ solves Problem $P_1$ when each component objective $w_e$ has derivative $w_e'=h_e$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A base is lexicographically optimal exactly when each lower weighted-level set is a tight member of the submodular system, equivalently when the corresponding dependence sets remain within those level sets, and equivalently when the base solves the associated separable optimization problem.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{(i)}\iff\text{(ii)}\iff\text{(iii)}\iff\text{(iv)}

children.title: Weighted Max–Min Models
children.top_down_role: Balance criteria prioritizing the largest achievable weighted minimum.

knowledge_statements.title: Weighted Max–Min Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Maximization of the smallest weighted allocation ratio over a polymatroid base.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:2^E\to\mathbb R_+\) be normalized, nondecreasing, and submodular, let \(w\in\mathbb R_{++}^E\), and let \(B(f)\) be nonempty. The weighted max–min value is
\[\alpha^*=\max_{x\in B(f)}\min_{i\in E}\frac{x_i}{w_i}=\min_{\varnothing\ne S\subseteq E}\frac{f(S)}{w(S)}.\]
Thus a scalar \(\alpha\) is attainable as a common lower ratio precisely when \(\alpha w(S)\le f(S)\) for every nonempty \(S\subseteq E\). Any maximizing base satisfies \(x_i/w_i\ge\alpha^*\) for all \(i\), with equality on at least one critical subset.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The largest guaranteed weighted allocation ratio equals the minimum density of a nonempty subset; its critical subsets identify max–min bottlenecks.
assumptions_latex: \(f(\varnothing)=0\), and \(f\) is nondecreasing, nonnegative, and submodular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\alpha^*=\min_{\varnothing\ne S\subseteq E}f(S)/w(S)\).

notation.meaning: The optimal minimum weighted allocation ratio.
The polymatroid base polytope of f.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation content kind fits the model leaf, and the density formula is plausible under the stated polymatroid assumptions. No citation is provided, however, so the exact lower-bound feasibility characterization and the claim about equality on a critical subset remain unverified.

children.title: Weighted Min–Max Models
children.top_down_role: Balance criteria prioritizing the smallest achievable weighted maximum.

knowledge_statements.title: Weighted Min–Max Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimization of the largest weighted allocation ratio over a polymatroid base.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:2^E\to\mathbb R\) be normalized and submodular, let \(w\in\mathbb R_{++}^E\), and suppose \(B(f)\ne\varnothing\). The weighted min–max value is
\[\beta^*=\min_{x\in B(f)}\max_{i\in E}\frac{x_i}{w_i}=\max_{\varnothing\ne S\subseteq E}\frac{f(E)-f(E\setminus S)}{w(S)}.\]
Equivalently, a scalar \(\beta\) admits a base satisfying \(x_i\le\beta w_i\) for every \(i\) if and only if \(f(E)-f(E\setminus S)\le\beta w(S)\) for every nonempty \(S\subseteq E\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The smallest possible largest weighted ratio equals the maximum complementary marginal density, giving an exact feasibility test for coordinatewise upper bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\beta^*=\max_{\varnothing\ne S\subseteq E}[f(E)-f(E\setminus S)]/w(S)\).

notation.meaning: The optimal maximum weighted allocation ratio.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation content kind is appropriate. The complementary marginal-density formula and coordinatewise upper-bound feasibility equivalence are nontrivial and have no cited theorem, section, or page; an authoritative source is required to confirm their hypotheses and scope.

children.title: Extremal-Balance Duality
children.top_down_role: Structural correspondence between the two weighted extremal criteria.

knowledge_statements.title: Extremal-Balance Duality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complementary transformation relating weighted max–min and min–max base problems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:2^E\to\mathbb R\) be normalized and submodular with nonempty \(B(f)\), and define the complementary submodular function \(f^\#(S)=f(E\setminus S)-f(E)\). Then \(B(f^\#)=-B(f)\). For every \(w\in\mathbb R_{++}^E\),
\[\min_{x\in B(f)}\max_{i\in E}\frac{x_i}{w_i}=-\max_{y\in B(f^\#)}\min_{i\in E}\frac{y_i}{w_i}.\]
Hence weighted min–max balancing for \(f\) is exactly weighted max–min balancing for its complementary base after sign reversal; optimal solutions correspond by \(y=-x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sign reversal maps a base to its complementary base and converts weighted min–max balancing exactly into weighted max–min balancing.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B(f^\#)=-B(f)\) and the displayed min–max value is the negative complementary max–min value.

notation.meaning: The complementary submodular function defined by f#(S)=f(E\S)−f(E).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The duality content kind exactly fits the leaf, and the sign-reversal formulation is internally consistent. Nevertheless, the base transformation and induced equality of extremal values are uncited nontrivial claims and require a specific authoritative locator.

children.title: Majorization Order
children.top_down_role: Comparison of base vectors through cumulative sorted-coordinate dominance.

knowledge_statements.title: Majorization Order
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical majorization for vectors having equal total sum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(x,y\in\mathbb R^n\), let \(x^\downarrow\) and \(y^\downarrow\) denote their coordinates sorted in nonincreasing order. The vector \(x\) is majorized by \(y\), written \(x\preceq_{\mathrm{maj}}y\), if
\[\sum_{i=1}^k x_i^\downarrow\le\sum_{i=1}^k y_i^\downarrow\quad(1\le k<n),\qquad \sum_{i=1}^n x_i=\sum_{i=1}^n y_i.\]
Thus \(x\preceq_{\mathrm{maj}}y\) means that \(x\) is no more dispersed than \(y\) while preserving the total sum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A vector is majorized by another when every proper leading sum of its decreasing rearrangement is smaller, while both totals agree.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\preceq_{\mathrm{maj}}y\) exactly when the displayed partial-sum inequalities and total-sum equality hold.

notation.meaning: The coordinates of x arranged in nonincreasing order.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition content kind and mathematical formulation match Majorization Order, including the equal-total condition. It cannot pass the citation check because source_refs is empty; a standard textbook definition with a section, definition, or page locator is required.

children.title: Decreasing Minimization
children.top_down_role: Lexicographic minimization of coordinates arranged in decreasing order.

knowledge_statements.title: Decreasing Minimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lexicographic minimization of decreasingly sorted coordinates over a fixed-sum feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty and suppose every \(x\in X\) has the same coordinate sum. A vector \(x^*\in X\) is decreasingly minimal in \(X\) if its nonincreasing rearrangement \((x^*)^\downarrow\) is lexicographically no larger than \(x^\downarrow\) for every \(x\in X\). Equivalently, one first minimizes the largest coordinate, then the second-largest coordinate among the remaining minimizers, and continues through all coordinates. Weighted decreasing minimization applies the same definition to the ratios \(x_i/w_i\) for fixed positive weights \(w_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A decreasingly minimal vector lexicographically minimizes its coordinates after sorting them from largest to smallest; the weighted form sorts coordinate-to-weight ratios.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty and has constant coordinate sum.
For the weighted form, \(w_i>0\) for every \(i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((x^*)^\downarrow\le_{\mathrm{lex}}x^\downarrow\) for every \(x\in X\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition content kind fits the leaf and the unweighted definition is precise. No source is cited, and the appended weighted-ratio variant requires verification because weighted decreasing minimization may use conventions that must be stated consistently with the surrounding theory.

children.title: Majorization-Minimization Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Equivalence boundaries between majorization minimality and decreasingly minimal bases.

knowledge_statements.title: Majorization-Minimization Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence of least majorization, decreasing minimization, and symmetric convex minimization on a base polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(B(f)\subseteq\mathbb R^E\) be a nonempty compact base polytope of a normalized submodular function. A base \(x^*\in B(f)\) is decreasingly minimal if and only if it is majorized by every \(x\in B(f)\). Equivalently, for every continuous symmetric convex function \(\Phi:\mathbb R^E\to\mathbb R\),
\[\Phi(x^*)\le \Phi(x)\qquad(x\in B(f)).\]
In particular, \(x^*\) minimizes every separable objective \(\sum_{i\in E}\varphi(x_i)\) with common convex \(\varphi\). If \(\Phi\) is strictly convex, its minimizer is unique and equals \(x^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a compact base polytope, the decreasingly minimal base is precisely the least-majorized base and minimizes every symmetric convex objective.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is normalized and submodular, and \(B(f)\) is nonempty and compact.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^*\preceq_{\mathrm{maj}}x\) for all \(x\in B(f)\) if and only if \(x^*\) is decreasingly minimal, implying universal symmetric-convex optimality.

notation.meaning: The compact base polytope of f.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem content kind fits the correspondence leaf, but the equivalence among decreasing minimality, least majorization, and universal symmetric-convex minimization is substantial and uncited. A source must also confirm existence and the exact uniqueness conclusion for strictly convex symmetric objectives on the stated class of base polytopes.

knowledge_statements.title: Fair Resource-Allocation Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polymatroid-base formulations of efficient and convexly balanced resource allocation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:2^E\to\mathbb R_+\) be normalized, nondecreasing, and submodular. An efficient feasible allocation is a vector \(x\in B(f)\), so every coalition receives at most \(f(S)\) and the entire resource \(f(E)\) is allocated. Given positive weights \(w_i\) and convex functions \(\varphi_i:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\), a fair allocation model is
\[\min_{x\in B(f)}\sum_{i\in E}w_i\varphi_i\!\left(\frac{x_i}{w_i}\right).\]
Choices such as a common strictly convex \(\varphi_i=\varphi\) produce balanced allocations; the quadratic choice yields the weighted lexicographically optimal base.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Efficient resource allocations form a polymatroid base, and separable convex penalties on weighted allocation ratios select balanced or lexicographically fair allocations.
assumptions_latex: \(f(\varnothing)=0\), and \(f\) is nondecreasing, nonnegative, and submodular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Fair allocation is represented as separable convex minimization over \(B(f)\).

notation.meaning: The set of efficient feasible allocations.
The entitlement or scaling weight of recipient i.
The convex imbalance penalty for recipient i.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation content kind is appropriate for this modeling topic. The base-polytope allocation formulation is coherent, but no source supports the interpretation as fairness or the claim that the stated convex choices produce balanced and weighted lexicographically optimal allocations.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Optimality of the Continuous Threshold Box
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A threshold-box characterization for continuous fair resource allocation over a real submodular base polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the continuous fair-allocation assumptions, let \(v_*\) and \(v^*\) be the optimal values of the associated max--min and min--max problems, and define \(l,u\in\mathbb R^E\) by \[l(e)=\min\{\alpha\in\mathbb R:h_e(\alpha)\ge v_*\},\qquad u(e)=\max\{\alpha\in\mathbb R:h_e(\alpha)\le v^*\}.\] Then \(v_*\le v^*\), \(l\le u\), and \[B_{\mathbb R}(f)_l^u:=\{x\in B_{\mathbb R}(f):l\le x\le u\}\ne\varnothing.\] Every \(x\in B_{\mathbb R}(f)_l^u\) is an optimal solution of \(P_3\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The associated max–min value does not exceed the min–max value, the induced coordinate thresholds are ordered, and the bounded portion of the real base polyhedron is nonempty. Every point in that bounded base is an optimal continuous fair allocation.
assumptions_latex: g:\mathbb R^2\to\mathbb R\text{ is nondecreasing in its first argument and nonincreasing in its second}
\forall e\in E,\ h_e:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\text{ is continuous, nondecreasing, and onto}
v_*,v^*,l,u\text{ are defined by the associated continuous max--min and min--max problems}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: v_*\le v^*,\quad l\le u,\quad B_{\mathbb R}(f)_l^u\ne\varnothing,\quad \forall x\in B_{\mathbb R}(f)_l^u,\ x\in\operatorname*{argmin}(P_3).

knowledge_statements.title: Submodular Flow Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Capacitated directed flows whose boundary vector belongs to a submodular base polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(D=(V,A)\) be a directed graph, let \(f:2^V\to\mathbb R\) be submodular with \(f(\varnothing)=f(V)=0\), and let \(\ell,u\in\overline{\mathbb R}^{A}\) satisfy \(\ell\le u\). For \(x\in\mathbb R^A\), define \(\partial x(S)=x(\delta^{\mathrm{in}}(S))-x(\delta^{\mathrm{out}}(S))\). A submodular flow is an arc vector satisfying
\[\ell_a\le x_a\le u_a\quad(a\in A),\qquad \partial x(S)\le f(S)\quad(S\subseteq V).\]
Because \(\partial x(V)=f(V)=0\), the boundary vector \(\partial x\) belongs to the base polyhedron \(B(f)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A submodular flow obeys arc bounds and requires every vertex-set net inflow to lie below a submodular boundary bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\) is feasible exactly when \(\ell\le x\le u\) and \(\partial x\in B(f)\).

notation.meaning: Net flow entering the vertex subset S.
The base polyhedron determined by f.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition content kind matches the Submodular Flow Models leaf, and the displayed constraints are consistent with the declared net-inflow convention. The local inventory contains no cited submodular-flow source, so the definition and sign convention require an authoritative section or definition locator.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Feasibility of a Submodular Flow Problem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines feasible flows and feasibility for a capacitated submodular-flow model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,A)\), let \(\underline c:A\to\mathbb R\cup\{-\infty\}\) and \(\bar c:A\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) satisfy \(\underline c(a)\leq\bar c(a)\) for every \(a\in A\), and let \(\rho:2^V\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be submodular with \(\rho(\varnothing)=\rho(V)=0\). A function \(\xi:A\to\mathbb R\) is a feasible flow if \(\underline c(a)\leq\xi(a)\leq\bar c(a)\) for every \(a\in A\) and \(\partial\xi\in\mathbf B(\rho)\). The problem \(\mathrm{MSFP}_1\) is feasible if it admits a feasible flow.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Given compatible lower and upper arc capacities and a normalized submodular function, a real-valued flow is feasible when it satisfies every capacity bound and its boundary vector belongs to the base polyhedron of the function. The submodular-flow problem is feasible when such a flow exists.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \xi\text{ is a feasible flow}\iff\left[\underline c(a)\leq\xi(a)\leq\bar c(a)\ (\forall a\in A)\right]\land\left[\partial\xi\in\mathbf B(\rho)\right];\quad \mathrm{MSFP}_1\text{ is feasible iff such a }\xi\text{ exists}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Crossing-submodular flows and their polyhedron
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines crossing families, crossing-submodular functions, submodular flows, and the extended-polymatroid representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let D=(V,A), let \mathcal C\subseteq 2^V be crossing, meaning that T,U\in\mathcal C, T\cap U\neq\varnothing, and T\cup U\neq V imply T\cap U,T\cup U\in\mathcal C, and let f:\mathcal C\to\mathbb R be crossing submodular: f(T)+f(U)\ge f(T\cap U)+f(T\cup U) for every such pair. A submodular flow is an x\in\mathbb R^A satisfying x(\delta^{\mathrm{in}}(U))-x(\delta^{\mathrm{out}}(U))\le f(U) for every U\in\mathcal C. Its feasible set P is the submodular flow polyhedron, equivalently P=\{x\in\mathbb R^A:Mx\in EP_f\}, where M is the V\times A incidence matrix and Mx is the excess vector.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a crossing family and a function submodular on crossing pairs, a submodular flow satisfies the prescribed net-inflow upper bound for every set in the family. The resulting polyhedron equivalently consists of arc vectors whose incidence-matrix excess vector belongs to the extended polymatroid of the function.
assumptions_latex: \forall T,U\in\mathcal C:\ (T\cap U\neq\varnothing\land T\cup U\neq V)\Rightarrow f(T)+f(U)\ge f(T\cap U)+f(T\cup U)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: P=\left\{x\in\mathbb R^A:\forall U\in\mathcal C,\ x(\delta^{\mathrm{in}}(U))-x(\delta^{\mathrm{out}}(U))\le f(U)\right\}=\{x\in\mathbb R^A:Mx\in EP_f\}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Submodular flow problem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear-cost flows with capacity bounds and a base-polyhedron boundary constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let $G=(V,A)$, let $\underline c:A\to\mathbb R\cup\{-\infty\}$ and $\bar c:A\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}$ be lower and upper capacity functions, and let $\gamma:A\to\mathbb R$. Let $\mathcal F$ be a crossing family containing $\varnothing$ and $V$, and let $f:\mathcal F\to\mathbb R$ be crossing-submodular with $f(\varnothing)=f(V)=0$ and $B(f)\ne\varnothing$. The submodular-flow problem is
$$\min_{\varphi:A\to\mathbb R}\sum_{a\in A}\gamma(a)\varphi(a)$$
subject to $\underline c(a)\leq\varphi(a)\leq\bar c(a)$ for every $a\in A$ and $\partial\varphi\in B(f)$. A feasible $\varphi$ is a submodular flow; an optimal feasible solution is an optimal submodular flow.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A submodular flow satisfies the arc-capacity bounds and has its graph boundary in the base polyhedron of the specified normalized crossing-submodular function. The associated problem minimizes linear arc cost.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \min\left\{\sum_{a\in A}\gamma(a)\varphi(a):\underline c(a)\leq\varphi(a)\leq\bar c(a)\ (a\in A),\ \partial\varphi\in B(f)\right\}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Intersecting and crossing submodular-flow feasibility criteria
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Decomposition forms of the submodular-flow feasibility condition for intersecting and crossing families.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Assume $\varnothing,V\in\mathcal F$ and $f(\varnothing)=f(V)=0$. If $f$ is intersecting-submodular on the intersecting family $\mathcal F$, then $P_S$ is feasible if and only if
$$(\kappa_{\underline c,\bar c})^\#(X)\leq\sum_{i\in I}f(X_i)$$
for every $X\subseteq V$ and every disjoint family $X_i\in\mathcal F$ satisfying $X=\bigcup_{i\in I}X_i$. If $f$ is crossing-submodular on the crossing family $\mathcal F$, then $P_S$ is feasible if and only if
$$(\kappa_{\underline c,\bar c})^\#(X)\leq\sum_{i\in I}\sum_{j\in J_i}f(X_{ij})$$
for every $X\subseteq V$, codisjoint family $(X_i)_{i\in I}$, and, for each $i$, disjoint family $(X_{ij})_{j\in J_i}$ for which all displayed function values are defined, such that $X=\bigcap_{i\in I}X_i$ and $X_i=\bigcup_{j\in J_i}X_{ij}$. Equivalently, the crossing case may be expressed using disjoint $X_i$ with $X=\bigcup_iX_i$ and codisjoint $X_{ij}$ with $X_i=\bigcap_jX_{ij}$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an intersecting-submodular system, feasibility is equivalent to the cut bound for every disjoint decomposition into members of the family. For a crossing-submodular system, feasibility is equivalent to the corresponding codisjoint-intersection of disjoint-decompositions condition, or to its stated dual form.
assumptions_latex: f\text{ is intersecting-submodular on an intersecting family, or crossing-submodular on a crossing family, as applicable}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: P_S\text{ is feasible}\iff\text{the applicable quantified decomposition inequality holds}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Potential certificate for optimal submodular flows
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary and sufficient reduced-cost and maximum-weight-base conditions for optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A submodular flow $\varphi:A\to\mathbb R$ for $P_S$ is optimal if and only if there exists $p:V\to\mathbb R$ such that, with
$$\gamma_p(a)=\gamma(a)+p(\partial^+a)-p(\partial^-a),$$
for every $a\in A$,
$$\gamma_p(a)>0\Rightarrow\varphi(a)=\underline c(a),\qquad \gamma_p(a)<0\Rightarrow\varphi(a)=\bar c(a),$$
and $\partial\varphi$ is a maximum-weight base of $B(f)$ with respect to $p$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible submodular flow is optimal exactly when a vertex potential makes every positive reduced-cost arc attain its lower capacity and every negative reduced-cost arc attain its upper capacity, while the flow boundary maximizes the potential weight over the base polyhedron.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Submodular-flow feasibility and integrality criterion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary and sufficient cut conditions for feasible capacitated submodular flows, with an integral-data conclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A feasible flow for $P_S$ exists if and only if
$$\forall X\in\mathcal D:\quad (\kappa_{\underline c,\bar c})^\#(X)\leq f(X),$$
equivalently,
$$\forall X\in\mathcal D:\quad \bar c(\Delta^-X)-\underline c(\Delta^+X)+f(X)\geq0,$$
where
$$\Delta^+X=\{a\in A:\partial^+a\in X,\ \partial^-a\in V\setminus X\},\qquad \Delta^-X=\{a\in A:\partial^-a\in X,\ \partial^+a\in V\setminus X\}.$$
Moreover, if $\bar c$, $\underline c$, and $f$ are integer-valued and $P_S$ is feasible, then an integral feasible flow exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A capacitated submodular flow exists exactly when every set in the specified domain satisfies either equivalent cut inequality. With integer-valued lower capacities, upper capacities, and submodular function, feasibility guarantees an integral feasible flow.
assumptions_latex: P_S\text{ is the submodular-flow problem defined by the stated capacities and }f
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\varphi\,[\underline c\leq\varphi\leq\bar c,\ \partial\varphi\in B(f)]\iff\forall X\in\mathcal D:\bar c(\Delta^-X)-\underline c(\Delta^+X)+f(X)\geq0;\quad \bar c,\underline c,f\text{ integer-valued and feasibility}\Rightarrow\exists\varphi\text{ integral and feasible}

children.title: Supermodular Flow Models
children.top_down_role: Flow models governed by supermodular boundary requirements.

knowledge_statements.title: Supermodular Flow Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Capacitated directed flows constrained by supermodular lower bounds on boundary values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(D=(V,A)\) be a directed graph, let \(p:2^V\to\mathbb R\) be supermodular with \(p(\varnothing)=p(V)=0\), and let \(\ell,u\in\overline{\mathbb R}^{A}\) satisfy \(\ell\le u\). With \(\partial x(S)=x(\delta^{\mathrm{in}}(S))-x(\delta^{\mathrm{out}}(S))\), a supermodular flow is an arc vector satisfying
\[\ell_a\le x_a\le u_a\quad(a\in A),\qquad \partial x(S)\ge p(S)\quad(S\subseteq V).\]
Equivalently, define \(f(S)=-p(V\setminus S)\). Then \(f\) is submodular, and the same constraints are \(\partial x(S)\le f(S)\) for every \(S\subseteq V\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A supermodular flow imposes lower bounds on every set’s net inflow; complementing vertex sets converts it to an equivalent submodular upper-bound model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\partial x(S)\ge p(S)\) for all \(S\) is equivalent to \(\partial x(S)\le -p(V\setminus S)\) for all \(S\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition content kind fits the model leaf, and the complement transformation is algebraically consistent with the stated boundary convention. Because no source is cited, an authoritative locator is required for the terminology, hypotheses, and equivalence with the submodular upper-bound formulation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Crossing-supermodular inflow-covering polyhedron
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines crossing supermodularity and the associated nonnegative directed-flow covering system; the digraph notation is inherited from the section setup.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let D=(V,A), let \mathcal C be a crossing family of subsets of V, and let g:\mathcal C\to\mathbb R. The function g is crossing supermodular if, whenever T,U\in\mathcal C satisfy T\cap U\neq\varnothing and T\cup U\neq V, one has g(T)+g(U)\le g(T\cap U)+g(T\cup U). The associated polyhedron is P=\{x\in\mathbb R^A:x_a\ge0\ \forall a\in A,\ x(\delta^{\mathrm{in}}(U))\ge g(U)\ \forall U\in\mathcal C\}.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A function on a crossing family is crossing supermodular when it satisfies the reversed submodular inequality on every crossing pair. The associated polyhedron contains nonnegative arc vectors whose inflow into each set meets its prescribed requirement.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: g\text{ is crossing supermodular iff }\forall T,U\in\mathcal C,\ (T\cap U\neq\varnothing\land T\cup U\neq V)\Rightarrow g(T)+g(U)\le g(T\cap U)+g(T\cup U),\quad P=\{x\in\mathbb R^A:x_a\ge0\ (a\in A),\ x(\delta^{\mathrm{in}}(U))\ge g(U)\ (U\in\mathcal C)\}

children.title: Complementary Boundary Representations
children.top_down_role: Transformational relations between submodular and supermodular boundary descriptions.

knowledge_statements.title: Complementary Boundary Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Upper submodular and complementary lower supermodular descriptions of a base polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(E\) be finite and let \(f:2^E\to\mathbb R\) be submodular with \(f(\varnothing)=0\). Define \(p(S)=f(E)-f(E\setminus S)\). Then \(p\) is supermodular, and the upper and lower boundary descriptions coincide:
\[
\{x\in\mathbb R^E:x(S)\le f(S)\text{ for all }S\subseteq E,\ x(E)=f(E)\}
=
\{x\in\mathbb R^E:x(S)\ge p(S)\text{ for all }S\subseteq E,\ x(E)=p(E)\}.
\]
Thus complementing index sets converts every upper boundary inequality into its equivalent lower boundary inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A submodular base has an equivalent lower-bound description obtained from the complementary supermodular function.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B(f)=\{x:x(S)\ge f(E)-f(E\setminus S)\ \forall S\subseteq E,\ x(E)=f(E)\}\).

notation.meaning: Sum of the coordinates indexed by S.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complementary upper/lower base-polyhedron identity is mathematically precise, and representation is the appropriate kind, but no cited source supports its placement or the specific neoflow boundary terminology.

knowledge_statements.title: Independent Flow Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Terminal-boundary interpretation using a polymatroid independence polytope.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
An independent flow model consists of a directed graph \(D=(V,A)\), arc bounds \(\ell,u\in\mathbb R^A\), terminals \(T\subseteq V\), and a normalized, nondecreasing, submodular rank function \(r:2^T\to\mathbb R_+\). A flow \(x\in\mathbb R^A\) is feasible when \(\ell\le x\le u\), flow is conserved on \(V\setminus T\), and its nonnegative terminal inflow vector \(y\) satisfies
\[
y(S)\le r(S)\quad\text{for every }S\subseteq T.
\]
Equivalently, the boundary vector belongs to the independence polytope \(P(r)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An independent flow has conserved interior flow and a nonnegative terminal boundary vector lying in a polymatroid independence polytope.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\) is feasible exactly when \(\ell\le x\le u\), interior conservation holds, and \(y\in P(r)\).

notation.meaning: Polymatroid independence polytope defined by r.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed definition is coherent, but “independent flow” has multiple meanings and the nonnegative terminal-inflow convention is not established for this taxonomy context. An authoritative definition is required.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Independent flow problem and truncated-base representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-value minimum-cost flows with submodular-polyhedron restrictions at disjoint entrance and exit sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let $G=(V,A;S^+,S^-)$ with disjoint $S^+,S^-\subseteq V$, capacities $\underline c,\bar c$, costs $\gamma$, and submodular systems $(\mathcal D^+,f^+)$ on $S^+$ and $(\mathcal D^-,f^-)$ on $S^-$. For $v^*\in\mathbb R$, an independent flow of value $v^*$ is a map $\varphi:A\to\mathbb R$ satisfying
$$\underline c(a)\leq\varphi(a)\leq\bar c(a),\quad \partial\varphi(v)=0\quad(v\notin S^+\cup S^-),$$
$$(\partial\varphi)^{S^+}\in P(f^+),\qquad -(\partial\varphi)^{S^-}\in P(f^-),\qquad \partial\varphi(S^+)=v^*.$$
The independent-flow problem minimizes $\sum_{a\in A}\gamma(a)\varphi(a)$. If these constraints are feasible, then $v^*\leq\min\{f^+(S^+),f^-(S^-)\}$. For the respective $(f^+(S^+)-v^*)$- and $(f^-(S^-)-v^*)$-truncations $\widehat f^+$ and $\widehat f^-$, constraints on the two terminal boundary vectors and their value may be replaced by
$$(\partial\varphi)^{S^+}\in B(\widehat f^+),\qquad -(\partial\varphi)^{S^-}\in B(\widehat f^-).$$
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An independent flow of prescribed value obeys the arc capacities, conserves flow outside the entrance and exit sets, and places the entrance and negated exit boundary vectors in their respective submodular polyhedra. Feasibility bounds the prescribed value by both full-set function values. Under feasibility, the terminal conditions can be represented using the stated truncated base polyhedra.
assumptions_latex: (\mathcal D^+,f^+)\text{ and }(\mathcal D^-,f^-)\text{ are submodular systems}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \min\left\{\sum_{a\in A}\gamma(a)\varphi(a):\underline c\leq\varphi\leq\bar c,\ \partial\varphi|_{V\setminus(S^+\cup S^-)}=0,\ (\partial\varphi)^{S^+}\in P(f^+),\ -(\partial\varphi)^{S^-}\in P(f^-),\ \partial\varphi(S^+)=v^*\right\}

knowledge_statements.title: Polymatroidal Flow Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Directed flows with submodular capacity constraints on incident arc sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A polymatroidal flow model consists of a directed graph \(D=(V,A)\) and, for every vertex \(v\), normalized, nondecreasing, submodular functions \(r_v^-:2^{\delta^-(v)}\to\mathbb R_+\) and \(r_v^+:2^{\delta^+(v)}\to\mathbb R_+\). A nonnegative arc vector \(x\) is feasible when it satisfies the prescribed conservation equations and
\[
x(F)\le r_v^-(F)\quad(F\subseteq\delta^-(v)),\qquad
x(F)\le r_v^+(F)\quad(F\subseteq\delta^+(v))
\]
for every vertex \(v\). Modular rank functions recover ordinary individual arc capacities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A polymatroidal flow replaces separate arc capacities by submodular capacity constraints on every vertex’s incoming and outgoing arc sets.
assumptions_latex: Each \(r_v^-\) and \(r_v^+\) is a polymatroid rank function.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x|_{\delta^-(v)}\in P(r_v^-)\) and \(x|_{\delta^+(v)}\in P(r_v^+)\) for every \(v\).

notation.meaning: Incoming and outgoing arc sets at v.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: This is a recognizable definition of a polymatroidal flow and the content kind fits, but no inspectable citation is supplied. The phrase “prescribed conservation equations” also leaves the balance data unspecified.

knowledge_statements.title: Network-Type Submodular Systems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Submodular divergence constraints coupled to an ordinary capacitated network.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(D=(V,A)\) be a finite directed graph, let \(\ell,u\in\mathbb R^A\), and let \(f:2^V\to\mathbb R\) be submodular with \(f(\varnothing)=f(V)=0\). For \(x\in\mathbb R^A\), define its divergence by \(b_x(v)=x(\delta^+(v))-x(\delta^-(v))\). The associated network-type submodular system is
\[
\ell\le x\le u,\qquad b_x(S)\le f(S)\quad(S\subseteq V).
\]
Because \(b_x(V)=0=f(V)\), its divergence vector lies in the base polyhedron \(B(f)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A network-type submodular system imposes ordinary arc bounds and submodular upper inequalities on the flow-divergence vector.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\ell\le x\le u\) and \(b_x\in B(f)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Submodular Flow Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Base-polyhedral representation of feasible network divergences.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a finite directed graph \(D=(V,A)\), arc bounds \(\ell\le u\), and submodular \(f:2^V\to\mathbb R\) with \(f(\varnothing)=f(V)=0\), the submodular-flow feasible set is represented by
\[
\mathcal F_f=\{x\in\mathbb R^A:\ell\le x\le u,\ b_x\in B(f)\}.
\]
Equivalently, \(x\in\mathcal F_f\) precisely when its divergence satisfies \(b_x(S)\le f(S)\) for every \(S\subseteq V\); the equality \(b_x(V)=f(V)=0\) is automatic.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A submodular flow is an arc-bounded network flow whose divergence vector belongs to a specified submodular base polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal F_f=\{x:\ell\le x\le u,\ b_x(S)\le f(S)\ \forall S\subseteq V\}\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The base-polyhedral formula is internally consistent and representation is the correct role, but no source supports the claimed submodular-flow representation within the named neoflow equivalence container.

children.title: Independent Flow Representation
children.top_down_role: The independence-system side of the equivalence.

knowledge_statements.title: Independent Flow Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affine polymatroid-base representation of the same boundary vectors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(q\in\mathbb R^V\) be modular and define \(r(S)=f(S)+q(S)\). Suppose \(r\) is normalized and nondecreasing. For every arc vector \(x\), put \(y=b_x+q\). Then the independent-flow representation of the submodular boundary condition is
\[
y\in P(r),\qquad y(V)=r(V).
\]
Indeed, this maximal-sum face of the independence polytope is \(B(r)\), and translation by \(q\) gives \(y\in B(r)\) exactly when \(b_x\in B(f)\). Arc bounds remain unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After a modular translation, a submodular divergence condition becomes membership in the maximal-sum face of a polymatroid independence polytope.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(b_x\in B(f)\iff b_x+q\in P(r)\text{ and }(b_x+q)(V)=r(V)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The modular-translation identity is mathematically plausible, but no source establishes that this maximal-sum polymatroid face is the intended “Independent Flow Representation” in the immutable equivalence context.

children.title: Submodular-to-Independent Conversion
children.top_down_role: Structural translation from submodular flows to independent flows.

knowledge_statements.title: Submodular-to-Independent Conversion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Modular translation from a submodular base constraint to a polymatroid-base face.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Input a finite ground set \(V\), a submodular function \(f\) with \(f(\varnothing)=0\), and a boundary vector \(b\). For each \(v\in V\), choose
\[
q_v\ge \max_{S\subseteq V\setminus\{v\}}\bigl(f(S)-f(S\cup\{v\})\bigr).
\]
Initialize \(r(\varnothing)=0\), set \(q(S)=\sum_{v\in S}q_v\), and define \(r(S)=f(S)+q(S)\) and \(y=b+q\). Output the independent constraints \(y\in P(r)\) and \(y(V)=r(V)\). The construction preserves feasibility because \(y\in B(r)\) exactly when \(b\in B(f)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Add sufficiently large modular weights to make the submodular function monotone, then translate the boundary vector and impose the corresponding polymatroid base-face constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(b\in B(f)\iff y=b+q\in P(r)\text{ and }y(V)=r(V)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed modular correction does make the translated submodular function nondecreasing, and algorithm is suitable for a conversion leaf. However, no source confirms that this construction is the intended named neoflow conversion.

children.title: Independent-to-Submodular Conversion
children.top_down_role: Structural translation from independent flows to submodular flows.

knowledge_statements.title: Independent-to-Submodular Conversion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inverse translation from a polymatroid base face to submodular boundary inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Input a polymatroid rank function \(r:2^V\to\mathbb R_+\), a modular vector \(q\in\mathbb R^V\), and an independent boundary vector \(y\) constrained by \(y\in P(r)\) and \(y(V)=r(V)\). Initialize \(f(\varnothing)=0\), define \(f(S)=r(S)-q(S)\), and set \(b=y-q\). Output the submodular boundary system
\[
b(S)\le f(S)\quad(S\subseteq V),\qquad b(V)=f(V).
\]
Subtracting a modular function preserves submodularity, and the output satisfies \(b\in B(f)\) exactly when the input lies on the base face of \(P(r)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Subtract the modular translation from both the rank function and boundary vector to recover an equivalent submodular base system.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y\in B(r)\iff y-q\in B(r-q)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Subtracting the same modular function from the rank function and boundary vector gives the stated base-polyhedron translation, but the record lacks a source tying this operation to the named neoflow conversion.

children.title: Independent Flow Representation
children.top_down_role: The independence-system side of the equivalence.

knowledge_statements.title: Independent Flow Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Independent-polytope constraints applied to incident flow vectors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(D=(V,A)\) carry a nonnegative flow \(x\). For each vertex \(v\), let \(r_v^-\) and \(r_v^+\) be polymatroid rank functions on \(\delta^-(v)\) and \(\delta^+(v)\), respectively. The independent-flow representation imposes
\[
x|_{\delta^-(v)}\in P(r_v^-),\qquad x|_{\delta^+(v)}\in P(r_v^+)
\]
for every \(v\), together with the required conservation equations. Thus each local incident-flow vector is independently feasible in its designated polymatroid, while shared arc coordinates couple adjacent vertices.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each incoming and outgoing incident-flow vector must lie in a designated polymatroid independence polytope, with shared arcs and conservation coupling the local systems.
assumptions_latex: Each local rank function is normalized, nondecreasing, and submodular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x|_{\delta^-(v)}\in P(r_v^-)\) and \(x|_{\delta^+(v)}\in P(r_v^+)\) for all \(v\).

notation.meaning: Restriction of x to coordinates in F.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The local independence-polytope constraints are coherent, but no source confirms that they constitute the intended independent-flow representation rather than merely a restatement of polymatroidal capacities.

children.title: Polymatroidal Flow Representation
children.top_down_role: The polymatroidal-boundary side of the equivalence.

knowledge_statements.title: Polymatroidal Flow Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Subset-inequality expansion of local independent-polytope membership.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Under the local rank functions \(r_v^-\) and \(r_v^+\), polymatroidal feasibility has the explicit representation
\[
x(F)\le r_v^-(F)\quad\text{for all }F\subseteq\delta^-(v),\qquad
x(F)\le r_v^+(F)\quad\text{for all }F\subseteq\delta^+(v),
\]
for every vertex \(v\), together with \(x\ge0\) and the specified conservation equations. These subset inequalities are exactly the defining inequalities of the local independence polytopes, so this representation and the local independent-flow representation have identical feasible arc vectors.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Expanding each local independence-polytope membership condition yields the subset capacity inequalities defining a polymatroidal flow.
assumptions_latex: Each local rank function is a polymatroid rank function.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x|_{\delta^\pm(v)}\in P(r_v^\pm)\iff x(F)\le r_v^\pm(F)\) for every corresponding subset \(F\).

notation.meaning: Either the incoming or outgoing arc set at v.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Expanding local independence-polytope membership into subset inequalities is mathematically standard and representation is the correct kind, but the named equivalence and its local taxonomy sense have no cited support.

children.title: Independent-to-Polymatroidal Conversion
children.top_down_role: Structural translation from independent flows to polymatroidal flows.

knowledge_statements.title: Independent-to-Polymatroidal Conversion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expansion of local polytope membership into submodular subset capacities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Input a directed graph \(D=(V,A)\), local rank functions \(r_v^-\) and \(r_v^+\), and independent constraints \(x|_{\delta^-(v)}\in P(r_v^-)\) and \(x|_{\delta^+(v)}\in P(r_v^+)\). For each vertex \(v\), initialize the same incident arc sets and replace each membership constraint by all inequalities
\[
x(F)\le r_v^-(F)\quad(F\subseteq\delta^-(v)),\qquad
x(F)\le r_v^+(F)\quad(F\subseteq\delta^+(v)).
\]
Retain nonnegativity and conservation unchanged. Output the resulting polymatroidal flow system; its feasible arc vectors are identical to those of the input system.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replace each local independence-polytope membership constraint by its complete family of submodular subset capacity inequalities.
assumptions_latex: Each \(r_v^-\) and \(r_v^+\) is a polymatroid rank function.
The graph and local ground sets are finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{ind}}=\mathcal F_{\mathrm{poly}}\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The conversion is a valid finite constraint expansion, but no source establishes it as the intended named conversion. The record also does not characterize that explicit expansion may contain exponentially many inequalities.

children.title: Polymatroidal-to-Independent Conversion

knowledge_statements.title: Polymatroidal-to-Independent Conversion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compression of complete subset capacities into local independence-polytope membership.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Input a polymatroidal flow system whose local constraints are \(x(F)\le r_v^-(F)\) for every \(F\subseteq\delta^-(v)\) and \(x(F)\le r_v^+(F)\) for every \(F\subseteq\delta^+(v)\). For each vertex \(v\), initialize the polytopes \(P(r_v^-)\) and \(P(r_v^+)\), remove the expanded subset inequalities, and impose
\[
x|_{\delta^-(v)}\in P(r_v^-),\qquad x|_{\delta^+(v)}\in P(r_v^+).
\]
Retain nonnegativity and conservation unchanged. Output the independent representation, interpreted through rank oracles when the inequality families are implicit.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compress every complete family of local polymatroid inequalities into membership in the corresponding independence polytope.
assumptions_latex: The supplied subset inequalities use polymatroid rank functions.
Each complete local subset family is represented explicitly or by a rank oracle.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{poly}}=\mathcal F_{\mathrm{ind}}\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Compression into polytope-membership notation is formally equivalent when the complete subset families come from the stated rank functions, but neither the named conversion nor the rank-oracle interpretation is sourced.

children.title: Polymatroidal Flow Representation
children.top_down_role: The polymatroidal-boundary side of the equivalence.

assumptions_latex: For each \(v\in V\), normalized nondecreasing submodular functions \(\rho_v^-\) and \(\rho_v^+\) are given on the arcs entering and leaving \(v\), respectively.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The feasible vectors are precisely the nonnegative flows satisfying all local polymatroid inequalities.

notation.meaning: Set of arcs entering or leaving vertex v
Sum of flow over an arc set F
Local incoming and outgoing polymatroid rank functions

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local-capacity polymatroidal flow model; equivalence to submodular flow is treated separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A polymatroidal flow representation consists of a vector \(x\in\mathbb{R}_+^A\) satisfying flow conservation \(x(\delta^-(v))=x(\delta^+(v))\) at every designated transshipment vertex and the local inequalities
\[
x(F)\leq \rho_v^-(F)\quad(F\subseteq\delta^-(v)),\qquad x(F)\leq \rho_v^+(F)\quad(F\subseteq\delta^+(v)).
\]
Each function is normalized by \(\rho_v^\pm(\varnothing)=0\), nondecreasing, and submodular. Terminals may instead have prescribed net imbalance. Thus each incident flow vector lies in a polymatroid, while conservation couples the local polymatroids through the arcs of \(D\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A polymatroidal flow obeys conservation while every subset of arcs incident to a vertex satisfies a capacity inequality supplied by a local submodular rank function.
knowledge_statements.title: Polymatroidal Flow Representation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits the leaf, and the formulation is plausible, but no citation supports the precise local-polymatroid model, terminal treatment, or terminology.

children.title: Submodular Flow Representation
children.top_down_role: The submodular-system side of the equivalence.

assumptions_latex: Arc bounds satisfy \(\ell(a)\leq u(a)\) for every \(a\in A\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Feasibility is represented by \(\ell\leq x\leq u\) and \(\partial x\in B(f)\).

notation.meaning: Sum of vector coordinates indexed by X

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Base-polyhedron formulation of bounded submodular flows.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define the base polyhedron
\[
B(f)=\{y\in\mathbb{R}^V:y(X)\leq f(X)\text{ for every }X\subseteq V,\ y(V)=f(V)\}.
\]
A submodular flow is an arc vector \(x\in\mathbb{R}^A\) such that
\[
\ell(a)\leq x(a)\leq u(a)\quad(a\in A),\qquad \partial x\in B(f).
\]
Equivalently, its net-inflow vector satisfies \((\partial x)(X)\leq f(X)\) for every \(X\subseteq V\), together with \((\partial x)(V)=0\). Linear-cost submodular flow additionally minimizes \(\sum_{a\in A}c(a)x(a)\) over this feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bounded submodular flow is an arc vector whose net-inflow vector belongs to the base polyhedron of a submodular set function.
knowledge_statements.title: Submodular Flow Representation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits and the base-polyhedron formulation is standard in appearance, but the record has no authoritative source for its sign convention, normalization, and exact definition.

children.title: Polymatroidal-to-Submodular Conversion
children.top_down_role: Structural translation from polymatroidal flows to submodular flows.

assumptions_latex: A finite polymatroidal flow instance has rational local rank functions accessible through value oracles.
The representation permits auxiliary vertices and arcs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The constructed submodular-flow instance preserves feasibility and projected arc flows.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Auxiliary-network conversion preserving the original arc-flow projection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A polymatroidal-to-submodular conversion replaces each local incoming or outgoing polymatroid constraint by an auxiliary vertex block and defines a submodular function \(f_{\mathcal P}\) on the enlarged vertex set so that
\[
x\text{ is feasible for }\mathcal P
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\exists z\text{ feasible for }\mathcal S(\mathcal P)\text{ with }\pi(z)=x.
\]
The construction retains the original arc variables, imposes ordinary bounds on auxiliary arcs, and encodes every local inequality \(x(F)\leq\rho_v^\pm(F)\) as a base-polyhedron inequality for \(f_{\mathcal P}\). For linear objectives placed on original arcs, the extension assigns zero cost to auxiliary arcs, so corresponding feasible solutions have equal objective value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Local polymatroid capacities can be encoded by auxiliary network elements and one submodular base constraint while preserving projected flows and linear costs.
knowledge_statements.title: Polymatroidal-to-Submodular Conversion

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source or explicit construction establishes that arbitrary local polymatroid constraints admit the asserted single-base-polyhedron realization while preserving projections and costs. The exact construction is also needed to decide whether this leaf should contain a representation or an algorithm.

children.title: Submodular-to-Polymatroidal Conversion
children.top_down_role: Structural translation from submodular flows to polymatroidal flows.

assumptions_latex: A finite rational submodular-flow instance is given through a value oracle for its defining function.
The representation permits auxiliary vertices, arcs, and local polymatroid constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The constructed polymatroidal instance preserves feasibility and projected arc flows.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Auxiliary-network realization of a global base-polyhedron constraint by local polymatroids.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A submodular-to-polymatroidal conversion constructs local rank functions on an enlarged directed network such that
\[
x\text{ is feasible for }\mathcal S
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\exists z\text{ feasible for }\mathcal P(\mathcal S)\text{ with }\pi(z)=x.
\]
The auxiliary variables route the net-inflow vector of the original arcs through local polymatroid constraints whose projection is the base polyhedron \(B(f)\). Original lower and upper bounds remain ordinary arc constraints. When the original objective is linear, original arcs retain their costs and auxiliary arcs receive zero cost; hence projection and extension preserve objective values and optimal solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A global submodular base constraint can be realized through auxiliary flows and local polymatroid capacities, preserving original flows and linear objective values.
knowledge_statements.title: Submodular-to-Polymatroidal Conversion

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The claimed realization of an arbitrary global base-polyhedron constraint by local polymatroids is specialized and unsupported. A cited construction is required to validate feasibility, projection, objective preservation, and the selected knowledge kind.

assumptions_latex: The arc bounds \(\ell,u\) are finite and satisfy \(\ell\leq u\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A feasible submodular flow exists exactly when every displayed cut inequality holds.

notation.meaning: Sum of bound values over an arc set

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite bounded base-polyhedron feasibility criterion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
There exists \(x\in\mathbb{R}^A\) satisfying \(\ell\leq x\leq u\) and \(\partial x\in B(f)\) if and only if
\[
\ell(\delta^-(X))-u(\delta^+(X))\leq f(X)
\qquad\text{for every }X\subseteq V.
\]
Necessity follows from the bound-implied inequality \((\partial x)(X)\geq\ell(\delta^-(X))-u(\delta^+(X))\) and the base inequality \((\partial x)(X)\leq f(X)\). The reverse implication is the submodular-flow feasibility min–max assertion under the stated finite submodular hypotheses.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bounded submodular flow exists exactly when each cut's forced minimum net inflow does not exceed the submodular allowance for that vertex set.
knowledge_statements.title: Feasibility Min–Max Framework

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem kind fits the framework leaf, and the displayed cut condition is plausible under the stated net-inflow convention, but the sufficiency theorem has no source. The statement also contains proof-style justification, which must be removed in any sourced revision.

children.title: Cut Certificates
children.top_down_role: Feasibility or obstruction witnesses expressed through network cuts.

assumptions_latex: The data \(D,f,\ell,u\) satisfy the finite bounded submodular-flow hypotheses.
A subset \(X\subseteq V\) is explicitly supplied.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A strict cut violation certifies infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Infeasibility witness for bounded submodular flow.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(X\subseteq V\), define
\[
d(X)=\ell(\delta^-(X))-u(\delta^+(X))-f(X).
\]
If \(d(X)>0\), then \(X\) is a cut certificate of infeasibility. Indeed, every vector satisfying the arc bounds has
\[
(\partial x)(X)\geq\ell(\delta^-(X))-u(\delta^+(X))>f(X),
\]
whereas membership of \(\partial x\) in \(B(f)\) requires \((\partial x)(X)\leq f(X)\). The certificate is checked by evaluating one submodular-function value and summing the lower and upper bounds on the two directed sides of the cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A vertex set certifies infeasibility when its forced minimum net inflow exceeds its submodular allowance; checking the witness requires one cut calculation.
knowledge_statements.title: Cut Certificates

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate kind fits, and a positive displayed deficit is a plausible infeasibility witness, but its governing feasibility framework is uncited. The statement includes proof text that should be removed when a sourced record is supplied.

children.title: Tight-Set Certificates
children.top_down_role: Witnesses expressed through saturated submodular constraints.

assumptions_latex: The vector \(y\) belongs to the base polyhedron \(B(f)\).
The subset \(X\subseteq V\) is explicitly supplied.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The equality \(y(X)=f(X)\) certifies that the base inequality indexed by \(X\) is active.

notation.meaning: Slack of the base inequality indexed by X

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Active-set witness inside a submodular base polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A set \(X\subseteq V\) is tight for \(y\in B(f)\) when
\[
s_y(X)=f(X)-y(X)=0.
\]
Thus \(X\) certifies an active base-polyhedron inequality by the verifiable equality \(y(X)=f(X)\). Moreover, submodularity implies that the tight-set family
\[
\mathcal T_y=\{X\subseteq V:y(X)=f(X)\}
\]
is closed under union and intersection: if \(X,Y\in\mathcal T_y\), then \(X\cup Y\in\mathcal T_y\) and \(X\cap Y\in\mathcal T_y\). Consequently, unions and intersections of supplied tight witnesses remain valid certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A tight-set certificate is a subset whose base-polyhedron inequality holds with equality; tight sets are closed under union and intersection.
knowledge_statements.title: Tight-Set Certificates

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate kind fits and the active-inequality definition is precise, but no source supports the asserted lattice closure of tight sets in this exact base-polyhedron setting.

children.title: Cut–Tight-Set Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Structural relations between network cuts and tight constraint families.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Zero exchange capacity is equivalent to the existence of a tight set containing \(u\) and excluding \(v\).

notation.meaning: Maximum feasible transfer from v to u in the base polyhedron
Slack of the inequality indexed by X

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Base-polyhedron exchange obstruction expressed by a separating tight set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define the exchange capacity
\[
\kappa_y(u,v)=\sup\{\alpha\geq0:y+\alpha(\chi_u-\chi_v)\in B(f)\}.
\]
Then
\[
\kappa_y(u,v)=\min\{f(X)-y(X):u\in X,\ v\notin X\}.
\]
Accordingly, \(\kappa_y(u,v)=0\) if and only if some tight set \(X\) satisfies \(u\in X\) and \(v\notin X\). Such a set is simultaneously a cut separating the proposed exchange endpoints and a tight base constraint blocking every positive transfer in that direction. Positive minimum slack permits an exchange of any size not exceeding that slack.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A proposed base-polyhedron exchange is blocked exactly when a tight set separates its receiving vertex from its giving vertex.
knowledge_statements.title: Cut–Tight-Set Correspondence

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property kind is reasonable for the correspondence leaf, but the exchange direction and minimum-slack formula require an authoritative locator. No cited evidence confirms the orientation or zero-capacity equivalence.

assumptions_latex: The vector \(x\) is feasible for a finite linear-cost submodular-flow instance.
The residual structure includes bound-residual arcs and admissible base-polyhedron exchange arcs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A feasible potential satisfying all reduced-cost inequalities certifies global optimality of \(x\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reduced-cost certificate for linear-cost submodular flow.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A potential \(p:V\to\mathbb{R}\) is an optimality certificate for \(x\) when every residual arc \(e=(u,v)\) in \(R_x\) satisfies
\[
c_x(e)+p(u)-p(v)\geq0.
\]
The residual arcs comprise forward and reverse adjustments allowed by the arc bounds together with directed exchanges allowed by positive base-polyhedron exchange capacity. Because potential terms sum to zero around every directed cycle, the displayed inequalities imply that every residual directed cycle has nonnegative total cost. Under the residual-cycle optimality theorem for linear-cost submodular flow, this certifies that no feasible adjustment decreases the objective and hence that \(x\) is globally optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A vertex potential certifies optimality when all ordinary residual and submodular-exchange arcs have nonnegative reduced cost.
knowledge_statements.title: Potential Optimality Certificates

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate kind fits, but the residual exchange arcs and their costs are not defined precisely enough to validate the reduced-cost inequalities. The global-optimality implication depends on an uncited specialized theorem.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Potential criterion for continuous M-convex submodular flows
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimality characterization and fixed-potential description of all optimal flows for the continuous problem MSFP_3.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f_a\in\mathcal C[\mathbf R\to\mathbf R]\) for every \(a\in A\), and let \(f\in\mathcal M[\mathbf R\to\mathbf R]\). A feasible flow \(\xi:A\to\mathbf R\) is optimal if and only if there exists \(p:V\to\mathbf R\) such that \(\xi(a)\in\arg\min f_a[\delta p(a)]\) for every \(a\in A\) and \(\partial\xi\in\arg\min f[-p]\). If a potential \(p\) satisfies these conditions for an optimal flow \(\xi\), then a feasible flow \(\xi'\) is optimal if and only if \(\xi'(a)\in\arg\min f_a[\delta p(a)]\) for every \(a\in A\) and \(\partial\xi'\in\arg\min f[-p]\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible continuous M-convex submodular flow is optimal exactly when a potential satisfies the arcwise and boundary minimization conditions. A potential certifying one optimum characterizes every other feasible optimum by those same conditions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\xi\text{ is optimal}\iff\exists p:V\to\mathbf R:\ [\forall a\in A,\ \xi(a)\in\arg\min f_a[\delta p(a)]]\land[\partial\xi\in\arg\min f[-p]]\), and any fixed \(p\) satisfying these conditions for one optimum characterizes all other feasible optima.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Potential criterion and optimal-set structure for integer M-convex submodular flows
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Potential optimality certificate, fixed-potential characterization, optimal-boundary geometry, and integer-potential conclusion for the integer problem MSFP_3.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f_a\in\mathcal C[\mathbf Z\to\mathbf R]\) for every \(a\in A\), and let \(f\in\mathcal M[\mathbf Z\to\mathbf R]\). A feasible integer flow \(\xi:A\to\mathbf Z\) is optimal if and only if there exists \(p:V\to\mathbf R\) such that \(\xi(a)\in\arg\min f_a[\delta p(a)]\) for every \(a\in A\) and \(\partial\xi\in\arg\min f[-p]\). If such a potential \(p\) certifies an optimal integer flow, then it characterizes every other feasible optimal integer flow by the same conditions. Moreover, \(\partial\Xi^*=\{\partial\xi\mid\xi\text{ is an optimal integer flow}\}\) is an \(M_2\)-convex set. If additionally \(f_a\in\mathcal C[\mathbf Z\to\mathbf Z]\) for every \(a\) and \(f\in\mathcal M[\mathbf Z\to\mathbf Z]\), then an integer-valued certifying potential exists and the set \(\Pi^*\) of integer-valued optimal potentials is L-convex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible integer M-convex submodular flow is optimal exactly when a real potential satisfies the arcwise and boundary minimization conditions. A potential certifying one optimum characterizes all feasible integer optima. Their boundaries form an M2-convex set, and integer-valued costs guarantee an integer optimal potential whose optimal-potential set is L-convex.
assumptions_latex: \(\xi:A\to\mathbf Z\text{ is a feasible integer flow}\)
\(f_a\in\mathcal C[\mathbf Z\to\mathbf Z]\quad(a\in A),\ f\in\mathcal M[\mathbf Z\to\mathbf Z]\) for the integer-potential and L-convexity conclusions
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\xi\text{ is optimal}\iff\exists p:V\to\mathbf R:\ [\forall a\in A,\ \xi(a)\in\arg\min f_a[\delta p(a)]]\land[\partial\xi\in\arg\min f[-p]]\); also \(\partial\Xi^*\) is \(M_2\)-convex, while integer-valued costs imply an integer certifying potential and an L-convex set \(\Pi^*\).
